job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let's explore how liquids behave in a circuit. Rohan, if we place two wires in distilled water, why doesn't the bulb glow? Rohan: I think it is because the circuit is broken since the bulb is off. Teacher: Not quite. Distilled water is a poor conductor because it lacks dissolved salts. If we add a pinch of salt, it conducts electricity. Priya, what about sugar? Priya: Adding sugar to water makes it a good conductor because the sugar dissolves. Teacher: Actually, sugar molecules do not break into charged ions, so it remains a poor conductor. Now, consider electroplating. When we coat an iron spoon with copper, the copper metal from the copper plate dissolves into the liquid as ions and then deposits onto the spoon. It is not that electricity turns into metal. The liquid acts as a medium for these ions to travel. Finally, if you see bubbles during electrolysis, it is not boiling. It is a chemical reaction producing gases like hydrogen or oxygen. Also, always check your LED connections; the longer lead must connect to the positive terminal, or it won't light up. Remember, the liquid is an active participant in the chemical change, not just a container.

items.evidence: Distilled water is a poor conductor because it lacks dissolved salts.
items.q: Why does a bulb stay off when two wires are placed in distilled water?
options: The water has no dissolved salts to carry current
The circuit is broken because the bulb is off
The wires are too far apart in the water
The water is too pure to be a liquid
items.explain: Distilled water lacks dissolved salts, so it is a poor conductor and cannot light the bulb.

wrong.why: thinks the bulb being off means the circuit is broken
blames wire distance, a nearby detail not in the passage
thinks pure water is a special kind of conductor

items.evidence: Actually, sugar molecules do not break into charged ions, so it remains a poor conductor.
items.q: Sugar dissolves completely in water, yet the bulb stays off. Which explains this?
options: Sugar does not split into charged particles
Sugar dissolves too slowly to matter
Sugar makes the water pure and distilled
Sugar is the same as dissolved salt
items.explain: Sugar molecules do not break into charged ions, so sugar water stays a poor conductor.

wrong.why: thinks any dissolved substance makes water conduct
guesses speed of dissolving matters, not ions
mixes up sugar water with distilled water

items.evidence: When we coat an iron spoon with copper, the copper metal from the copper plate dissolves into the liquid as ions and then deposits onto the spoon.
items.q: How does copper reach the iron spoon during electroplating?
options: It moves through the liquid as ions
It jumps through the air to the spoon
It is made new from the electricity
It is already hidden inside the spoon
items.explain: Copper dissolves from the plate as ions, travels through the liquid and deposits on the spoon.

wrong.why: thinks atoms jump through air between plates
invents a source of copper inside the spoon

items.evidence: Finally, if you see bubbles during electrolysis, it is not boiling. It is a chemical reaction producing gases like hydrogen or oxygen.
items.q: Bubbles appear at the wires in a water tester. What are they?
options: Gases made by a chemical reaction
Steam made as the water boils
Air that was trapped in the wires
Dirt that was lifted off the plates
items.explain: Bubbles in electrolysis are gases like hydrogen or oxygen from a chemical reaction, not boiling.

wrong.why: thinks the bubbles are boiling water
thinks bubbles are only trapped air

items.evidence: Remember, the liquid is an active participant in the chemical change, not just a container.
items.q: In electroplating, what would change if plain dry air replaced the liquid?
options: Ions could not travel, so no plating
Nothing, as the liquid only holds plates
The plating would be faster and thicker
The plates would turn into magnets
items.explain: The liquid is an active participant that lets ions travel, so without it no plating can happen.

wrong.why: thinks the liquid is only a container
thinks removing the liquid helps the process
